nodes.title: Jerusalem, tribes, and David’s thrones

payload.title: Follow Jerusalem

payload.description: Hold Sirach’s praise, Maccabean exhortation, Kings’ evaluation, and Samuel’s difficult close together.

nodes.note: David is placed after Nathan, compared to fat separated from an offering, remembered for beasts and Goliath, praised for songs, and credited with arranging festival worship.
nodes.title: Sirach remembers lion, bear, Goliath, praise, and worship

nodes.note: The portrait says the Lord took away David’s sins, exalted his power, gave a covenant and throne, then moves through Solomon’s wisdom, desire, and the kingdom’s division.
nodes.title: Sirach retains pardon, covenant, and the division after David

nodes.note: Mattathias calls his sons to zeal and fidelity, names ancestors as examples, says David inherited a royal throne because he was merciful, assigns leadership, and dies.
nodes.title: A deathbed exhortation remembers David’s mercy

nodes.note: Abijam’s sins and heart are contrasted with David, while a lamp in Jerusalem is preserved for David’s sake and Uriah is named as David’s exception.
nodes.title: Abijam is measured against David’s heart

nodes.note: Gad directs an altar; Araunah offers place, animals, and wood, but David insists on purchase, pays fifty silver shekels for floor and oxen, sacrifices, and the plague is stopped.
nodes.title: David buys the threshing floor and builds an altar

payload.title: Follow later portraits of David

payload.description: Move through the cave, Abigail’s intervention, the camp, and the later contrast of royal taking.

nodes.note: David cuts Saul’s robe, is struck in heart, restrains his men, speaks from a distance, and receives Saul’s recognition and requested oath.
nodes.title: Power is restrained in the cave

nodes.note: Nabal refuses David’s request, David arms his men, Abigail acts quickly with provisions and speech, David blesses her intervention, and Nabal dies.
nodes.title: Abigail interrupts bloodshed

nodes.note: David and Abishai enter Saul’s camp, take spear and water jar, refuse to strike the anointed king, and call across the distance until Saul blesses David.
nodes.title: Saul is spared in the camp

nodes.note: At the season when kings go out, David remains in Jerusalem, sees a woman bathing, asks who she is, sends messengers, takes her, and receives word of pregnancy.
nodes.title: The king remains, sees, sends, and takes

payload.title: Follow restraint and interrupted violence

payload.description: Observe how later kings are measured, protected, judged, or reformed through remembered David.

nodes.note: Foreign wives turn Solomon toward other gods; the LORD is angry and announces a torn kingdom while preserving one tribe for David and Jerusalem.
nodes.title: Solomon’s divided heart is measured against David

nodes.note: Abijam’s sins and heart are contrasted with David, while a lamp in Jerusalem is preserved for David’s sake and Uriah is named as David’s exception.
nodes.title: Abijam is measured against David’s heart

nodes.note: Hezekiah removes high places and the bronze serpent, trusts the LORD, keeps commands, and is said to do right according to David.
nodes.title: Hezekiah is measured through David

nodes.note: The psalm praises steadfast love, recalls covenant with David, expands God’s rule, quotes the promise, then laments rejection, broken walls, shortened youth, and asks how long.
nodes.title: Covenant praise turns into protest over the crown

payload.title: Follow the royal standard

payload.description: Read the battle account, the messenger’s claim, David’s judgment, and the lament as separate evidence.

nodes.note: Israel flees, Saul’s sons fall, Saul is wounded and dies on his sword, the armor bearer follows, and Jabesh Gilead retrieves and buries the bodies.
nodes.title: Saul dies on Mount Gilboa

nodes.note: A messenger arrives with torn clothes, reports Israel’s defeat, claims he killed Saul at Saul’s request, presents the crown, and is executed after David questions him.
nodes.title: An Amalekite claims Saul’s death before David

nodes.note: The song names Israel’s beauty, Gilboa, weapons, Saul and Jonathan together, the daughters of Israel, and Jonathan’s love.
nodes.title: David teaches a lament for Saul and Jonathan

payload.title: Follow Saul’s death and David’s response

payload.description: Keep service, friendship, marriage, pursuit, covenant, mercy, and later household memory in view.

nodes.note: Saul’s servants seek a skilled musician; David arrives with gifts, becomes armor bearer, and plays when Saul is troubled.
nodes.title: Music brings David into Saul’s court

nodes.note: Jonathan binds himself to David, women sing of victory, Saul grows angry and afraid, and David continues to act wisely before the people.
nodes.title: Love, praise, and hostility arrive together

nodes.note: Saul’s anger at the new-moon meal exposes his intent; Jonathan shoots the signal, dismisses the boy, and parts from David after oath and grief.
nodes.title: The arrows confirm that David must leave

nodes.note: David cuts Saul’s robe, is struck in heart, restrains his men, speaks from a distance, and receives Saul’s recognition and requested oath.
nodes.title: Power is restrained in the cave

nodes.note: David seeks a survivor of Saul’s house for Jonathan’s sake, restores Saul’s land to Mephibosheth, seats him at the royal table, and appoints Ziba’s household to work the land.
nodes.title: Power remembers Jonathan’s covenant

payload.title: Follow Saul’s house

payload.description: Track the king’s verbs, intermediaries, Uriah’s resistance, arranged death, and Nathan’s retelling.

nodes.note: At the season when kings go out, David remains in Jerusalem, sees a woman bathing, asks who she is, sends messengers, takes her, and receives word of pregnancy.
nodes.title: The king remains, sees, sends, and takes

nodes.note: David summons Uriah, asks about the war, repeatedly sends him home, offers a gift, makes him drunk, and hears Uriah name ark, Israel, Judah, and soldiers in tents.
nodes.title: Uriah refuses the comforts David arranges

nodes.note: David writes Uriah’s death order and sends it by Uriah, Joab positions him, soldiers die, a report is managed, Bathsheba mourns, David takes her into his house, and the LORD is displeased.
nodes.title: A sealed order turns battle into arranged death

nodes.note: Nathan tells of a rich man taking a poor man’s ewe, David condemns the act, Nathan says “You are the man,” recounts gifts and taking, announces consequences, and receives confession.
nodes.title: Nathan’s story turns David’s judgment on himself

payload.title: Follow sending and taking

payload.description: Trace mercy cries, public acclaim, lineage answers, and Jesus’ question about David’s Lord.

nodes.note: The men follow Jesus crying for mercy, answer his question about belief, receive touch and sight, and spread the report despite a warning.
nodes.title: Two blind men call Jesus Son of David

nodes.note: The woman cries for mercy and her daughter, meets silence and disciple pressure, debates lost sheep and household crumbs, is commended for faith, and her daughter is healed.
nodes.title: A Canaanite woman calls the Son of David

nodes.note: The crowd tries to silence two men who call Jesus Lord and Son of David; Jesus stops, asks their desire, touches their eyes, and they follow.
nodes.title: Two blind men call from the Jericho road

nodes.note: A blind beggar hears Jesus is passing, cries “Son of David,” persists through rebuke, throws off his cloak, names his request, receives sight, and follows on the way.
nodes.title: Bartimaeus calls Jesus Son of David

nodes.note: Jesus rides into Jerusalem, crowds use royal psalm language, the city asks who he is, Temple commerce is overturned, blind and lame people are healed, and children cry “Hosanna to the son of David.”
nodes.title: Son of David cries enter Jerusalem and the Temple

nodes.note: Pharisees answer that the Christ is David’s son; Jesus cites David speaking by the Spirit in Psalm 110 and asks how the son is also called Lord.
nodes.title: Jesus asks how the Christ is David’s son and Lord

payload.title: Follow “Son of David”

payload.description: Read the Samuel song, Psalm 18, last words, and later Davidic psalm citations without assuming one editorial setting.

nodes.note: David sings of rock, distress, cosmic response, rescue, paths, combat, peoples, and steadfast love to the king and his offspring.
nodes.title: David interprets deliverance in a long song

nodes.note: The psalm moves through love, refuge, distress, cosmic descent, rescue, paths, conflict, peoples, and steadfast love to the king and offspring.
nodes.title: Deliverance is sung again as a psalm

nodes.note: David identifies himself through ancestry, anointing, song, and divine speech; just rule is compared to morning light and an everlasting covenant is named beside worthless thorns.
nodes.title: Last words join spirit, rule, and covenant

nodes.note: Peter speaks of Jesus’ death and resurrection, quotes David from Psalm 16, distinguishes David’s tomb, recalls the oath about his throne, and cites Psalm 110 before naming Jesus Lord and Christ.
nodes.title: Peter reads David’s psalm through resurrection and throne

payload.title: Follow the song into the Psalter

payload.description: Keep David’s final charge, the contested public anointing, the assembly retelling, and Solomon’s established throne in their distinct settings.

nodes.note: David renews his oath, commands Solomon ride the royal mule to Gihon, Zadok and Nathan anoint him, the city rejoices, Adonijah’s feast collapses, and Solomon grants conditional mercy.
nodes.title: David orders Solomon’s public anointing

nodes.note: David tells Solomon to be strong, keep the LORD’s charge, and deal wisely with Joab, Barzillai’s sons, and Shimei; he dies, is buried, and Solomon’s throne is established.
nodes.title: David charges Solomon and dies

nodes.note: David gathers leaders, recounts his desire and God’s choice, charges Israel and Solomon, gives plans and weights, and tells Solomon to be strong because God and organized workers are with him.
nodes.title: David gives Solomon plans before the assembly

nodes.note: David blesses God, asks who can give, prays for the people and Solomon, leads worship, witnesses Solomon’s enthronement, and dies after a full life and long reign.
nodes.title: Prayer, enthronement, and death close Chronicles’ David

payload.title: Follow the succession

payload.description: Trace site, material, divisions, plans, gifts, prayer, and Solomon’s later claim about David’s desire.

nodes.note: The angel directs Gad, David buys the place for six hundred gold shekels, builds an altar, receives fire from heaven, sees the sword sheathed, and fears to go to Gibeon.
nodes.title: Fire answers at Ornan’s threshing floor

nodes.note: David names the place as God’s house, assembles workers and materials, tells Solomon that warfare prevented his own building, and charges leaders to seek God and build.
nodes.title: David identifies the Temple site and prepares for Solomon

nodes.note: David makes Solomon king, gathers leaders, counts Levites, assigns service, and explains that the LORD has given rest and the ark will no longer be carried.
nodes.title: Levites are counted for a settled house

nodes.note: David gathers leaders, recounts his desire and God’s choice, charges Israel and Solomon, gives plans and weights, and tells Solomon to be strong because God and organized workers are with him.
nodes.title: David gives Solomon plans before the assembly

nodes.note: David names Solomon’s youth and the palace’s scale, gives his own treasure, asks who will offer willingly, and leaders respond until the people rejoice.
nodes.title: David and the assembly give for the house

nodes.note: Solomon blesses Israel, recounts God’s choice of David and Jerusalem, says he has built what David desired, and asks that the throne word be confirmed.
nodes.title: Solomon names the promise fulfilled and still asks for it

payload.title: Follow Temple preparation
